questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Luxembourg?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Luxembourg on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Luxembourg article.

questions.proof: The countries next to Luxembourg are Belgium, Germany, and France.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Luxembourg?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Luxembourg article.

questions.proof: The main language is Luxembourgish but French and German is also spoken there.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Luxembourg?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Luxembourg article.

questions.proof: Luxembourg officially called the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg is a landlocked country in Western Europe.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Between 1914 to 1918, Luxembourg was conquered by _____ during World War I.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “during”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Luxembourg article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Between 1914 to 1918, Luxembourg was conquered by Germany during World War I.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was ruled by the king of the _____.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Luxembourg article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: It was ruled by the king of the Netherlands.
